_comment: sCure version registry - newest first. On every release: bump the VERSION file at the repo root AND add an entry here (version, date, notes). The Settings > Versions modal shows this list.

notes: tools/error-editor.html is now the languages & errors editor (user, 2026-11-13: one JSON for every language, and the editor arranged by the languages): it loads sCureBox-CS config/errors.json (the English error registry) and/or config/languages.json (every UI language in one file). A language selector lists English plus every language in the file with how much is translated; English edits title / description / steps / support URL / video in errors.json as before (and keeps the English of languages.json in step); any other language edits its translation of the errors (Critical / Warnings), the 775 screen texts and the 59 firmware messages, each beside the English, with search, right-to-left fields for Hebrew, and live checks - placeholders that must survive, the same number of troubleshooting steps, texts still in English listed first. + Add language creates a new entry. Saves errors.json and languages.json separately.
Tests: the editor's logic was run on the real files (node, stub DOM): 10 languages, 918/918 texts each, 0 problems; Hebrew error cards render right to left.

DVT-SAF-017 (voltage selector in the mid position): the manual inspection step 'confirm no protective device operated and no damage occurred' (fuse_opened, visible_damage) is removed from the test and its pass criteria - not needed (user, 2026-11-12). Catalog 0.63 (English and Hebrew). The run no longer asks those two questions.
Tests: test_dvt_tool - SAF-017 passes on the machine's numbers whatever was recorded for fuse_opened / visible_damage.

DVT-SAF-003 (heater temperature sensor replaced by a fixed 10 kOhm resistor - frozen plausible reading) removed from the campaign (user, 2026-11-12): catalog 0.62 (English and Hebrew) - 42 tests, 317 runs; its script, process figure and catalog entry are gone, and DVT-SAF-020 no longer collects codes from it. The historical rename DVT-SAF-003 -> DVT-012 (2026-10-25 running numbers) stays so old records still map.
Tests: test_dvt_tool / test_dvt_web updated (run set 317, no DVT-SAF-003); the wizard's alarm-lock test now runs on DVT-SAF-017 (9007, voltage selector) instead.

DVT-SAF-011 (controller link lost): after the CM5 cable is pulled the runner watches the heater body for up to 10 min (was 4) - on the unit the body takes at least 5 min to turn down (user, 2026-11-12). The watch still ends 30 s after the body has clearly turned. The pass criterion heater_off_time <= 80 s is unchanged.

DVT-SAF-001: the reconnect step no longer waits for Done - it says 'RECONNECT the circulation fan supply' and goes on when the machine sees FAN_HEATER turn again (>= 300 RPM; a fan the trip left at 0 % is commanded to 30 %, the cooldown duty, so its tach can be read). If the tach never comes back within 5 min it falls back to asking for Done. The 60 s check that the alarm waits for an acknowledgement starts from the moment the fan was seen (user, 2026-11-12).
Tests: test_dvt_web - SAF-001 passes with no Reconnect/Done prompt; with no tach it falls back to Done.

DVT steps ("do this, then press I did it") look back: a step is done when the machine saw the change at any moment since the instruction appeared AND the person pressed, not only when the reading is still true at the moment the press arrives. The press travels through sCure Cloud for seconds; a door opened and let go had swung back by then and the press was not taken (user, 2026-11-12, DVT-SAF-008 on CureBox-3).
Tests: test_dvt_web test_saf012_takes_a_late_press_when_the_machine_saw_the_door_open_earlier (press arrives 100 polls late, door already shut).

DVT runner: a re-test (Run from sCure Cloud on a test already recorded) now starts from an empty record. 0.9.124 kept the old values and verdict, so the engine saw a finished run and ended at once with the old FAIL, without doing a step (user, 2026-11-12, DVT-SAF-008 on CureBox-3: 'done FAIL' 40 s after Start).
Tests: runner.test.cjs - the re-test's record has none of the old values and not the old FAIL.

DVT runner: Run from sCure Cloud on a test whose every run is already recorded (PASS / FAIL / BLOCKED / WAIVED) now runs it again - the confirmation goes to the machine and the new result replaces the old one on the machine (the portal keeps every published run). Before, the request ended at once as 'every run is already recorded' and nothing reached the machine (user, 2026-11-12: DVT-SAF-008 on CureBox-3 could not be started again after its FAIL).
Tests: runner.test.cjs - a recorded FAIL is offered again at the machine.

DVT-SAF-008 (door interlock) now has four steps: step 5 (the door status follows the door only, door_status_check) and step 6 (the alarm and error code of the interrupted cure, door_alarm_check) were removed (user, 2026-11-12). The pass criteria no longer include door_status_read_only_confirmed and alarm_raised; the fields door_status_read_only_confirmed, alarm_raised and error_code are gone from the test. Catalog 0.61 (English and Hebrew).

Found on the same run on CureBox-3: the step-6 error code was recorded as 'critical, warning, at, 6016' because the machine's ui_alerts holds the screen's alert counts, not codes - moot now that step 6 is removed.
Tests: test_dvt_web - the four-step run passes on a good door with four traces and no step-5/6 fields; guided sequence ends after the magnet step.

DVT runner: every call to sCure Cloud has a deadline (25 s; a long poll its hold time plus 25 s, cfg.portalTimeoutSec), and the run's report loop makes one try per report instead of four with pauses. A hung Apps Script execution had no limit (Node's own is 5 min), so the loop that carries the site's "I did it" presses to the machine stalled and the presses never arrived (user, 2026-11-12, DVT-SAF-008 step 4 on CureBox-3: pressed several times, run stopped after 120 s). A call slower than 8 s is logged as [slow].
Tests: runner.test.cjs - a report that never answers is cut at its deadline and the press still reaches the engine.

DVT step instructions ("do this, then press I did it"): a press is now kept for the whole step. The instruction text changes while the step waits ("- pressed, but the machine does not see it yet" / "- the machine sees it"), and each change cleared the press, so a press given before the machine saw the door was lost.

When the machine saw the change but nobody pressed "I did it", the run now says exactly that ('the machine saw it, but nobody pressed "I did it" within 120 s - ...'). Before, it said 'the machine did not see the door open' while the door sensor read OPEN (user, 2026-11-12, DVT-SAF-008 step 4 on CureBox-3).
DVT-SAF-008: the two 'OPEN the door' steps give the person 120 s instead of 30 s.
Tests: test_dvt_web test_saf012_says_the_press_is_missing_when_the_machine_saw_the_door (operator who never presses on step 4).

DVT runner: a test started from sCure Cloud now always gets its verdict. Scripts marked autoRecord: false (DVT-THM-001, DVT-THM-007 and ~10 others) leave the verdict to the operator's Record press in the DVT tool; the runner on the machine has no such press, so such a run reached the portal with an empty verdict and the request closed as 'done' - on 2026-11-09 DVT-THM-007 on UUT-02 measured a 9.29 C spread (limit 5) and was never marked FAIL. The runner now records the verdict itself when the script finished on its own (status OK, not stopped from the site). Test: runner.test.cjs case 1b.
That run (request 46, DVT-THM-007|UUT-02|setpoint=80,mains_voltage=220|1) was repaired by hand: verdict FAIL committed in the unit's results.json and re-sent to the portal.

New DVT test DVT-THM-007 'Chamber Heating Uniformity' (user, 2026-11-09), catalog 0.60, Performance phase after DVT-THM-001: one row - 80 C at 220 V only, once per unit (+5 runs). Fully automatic, no operator question: the runner records ambient and the start temperature, steps the chamber to 80 C, logs the control sensor and the 16-point TC-08 grid from the machine every second (traces heat_up and grid), records heat_up_time (control sensor first at 80 C, at most 60 min) and reached_setpoint, holds 80 C for 5 minutes, stops heating and computes uniformity_pp / uniformity_sd / grid_mean / hottest_position / coldest_position over the hold. Pass: reached_setpoint == true AND uniformity_pp <= 5 (CONFIRM; the heat-up time is recorded, not judged, until REQ-48 is settled).
English + Hebrew catalog, figure spec, dvt-catalog.js and SIM_PROMPTS rebuilt; tests test_thm007_chamber_heating_uniformity_runs_by_itself_at_220v and the run-set count (43 tests, 322 runs).

sCure Cloud redeployed (web app version @69, PORTAL_BUILD 0.9.147 so open tabs reload). The DVT runner on UUT-02 / CureBox-2 (sCureBox-CS 1.0.165) pushed catalog 0.60 at start, so the DVT tab lists DVT-THM-007.

DVT-THM-001 reads the 16-point chamber grid from the machine and computes the uniformity itself (user, 2026-11-09). Both TC-08s go on the machine's USB (sCureBox-CS 1.0.163 reports them in /api/dev/picolog/status units[]); the runner maps TC-08 0031 CH1-8 to Z1-Z2 and TC-08 114 CH1-8 to Z3-Z4, logs all 16 every second through the heat-up, soak and descent (trace 'grid'), and over the last 20 minutes of the soak - the same window as the steady-state error - takes each thermocouple's mean and records uniformity_pp (max - min of the 16 means), uniformity_sd (sample standard deviation of the means), hottest_position and coldest_position (Z<level>-<pos>). A note on the run lists all 16 means. A missing logger is said at the start; if the grid is still incomplete at the end the four values are asked by hand as before.

Simulator: the sim machine reports both loggers with fixed offsets per point; new test test_thm001_uniformity_is_computed_from_the_16_point_grid_on_the_machine. SIM_PROMPTS rebuilt (THM-001 now asks only the selector position).

DVT catalog 0.59: DVT-THM-001 (chamber heat-up / uniformity) now states the thermocouple grid (user, 2026-11-09) - 2 x 2 x 4, four levels Z1 (top) to Z4 (bottom), in each level 1 = back left, 2 = front left, 3 = back right, 4 = front right. TC-08 0031 holds the upper eight (CH1-4 = Z1, CH5-8 = Z2), TC-08 114 the bottom eight (CH1-4 = Z3, CH5-8 = Z4). hottest_position / coldest_position are written as Z<level>-<pos>. English and Hebrew catalogs, dvt-catalog.js rebuilt; dvt-auto.js VERSION brought back in step with VERSION.

io_controller (py + cpp): Left UV sensor on U6 AIN2, Temp Back on U7 AIN0 (user, 2026-11-01 - the 2026-10-01 swap undone), and the ORIGIN thermistor names renamed: TEMP_LEFT_ORIGIN -> TEMP_LEFT_UV, TEMP_RIGHT_ORIGIN -> TEMP_RIGHT_UV, TEMP_BACK_ORIGIN -> TEMP_BACK, TEMP_DOOR_ORIGIN -> TEMP_DOOR - in io_bridge, the control dashboards, the QA tool, errors.json (9011 / 9012 now 'Left / Right UV Temperature Sensor Disconnected') and the SRS. HSI sCure (3).xlsx updated to match (backup 'before UV-sensor rename 2026-11-01'); same change as sCureBox-CS 1.0.139.

sCure Cloud: sign in with a Google account instead of the shared password (user, 2026-10-30), and a people list where each person has an access: Viewer (sees everything, changes nothing), Service (also requests / cancels / answers DVT tests, sends programs to a machine, edits DVT units and the race) or Admin (also approves electrical-safety runs and manages people). The server checks the access on every action, not only the screen; a refused action says which access it needs.

Admins get a People screen (header button): add someone by Google email with a name and an access, change the access in the list, remove someone (their open session stops at once). The owner (OWNER_EMAIL) and the last admin cannot be removed. Recent activity (sign-ins, refusals, every change and every service / admin action) is kept in the 'audit' sheet and shown under a fold.

Turning it on: a Google Cloud OAuth client (Web application) with the web app's /exec URL as redirect URI, then GOOGLE_CLIENT_ID and GOOGLE_CLIENT_SECRET in the script properties - the People screen shows the exact URI. Until then the shared password still signs in, as an admin; once on, the password no longer works. An approval of a safety run is signed with the signed-in person's name and email.

Tests: test_code.cjs (sign-in round trip with Google played by the test, refusals - not on the list, unverified, other app, expired, cancelled, made-up state - every action per access, role change / removal taking effect at once, last admin, audit) and test_people.cjs (browser: the Google button, the header, adding / changing / removing people, a viewer refused, phone width).

DVT: every action a person performs is confirmed with a press. An instruction published by a guided script (c.act / the new c.doThis) carries an 'I did it' button - 48 px, on the phone too - and the script goes on only when BOTH hold: the person pressed it AND, where the machine can see the action, the machine agrees. The press never stands in for a reading: while they disagree the step says which half is missing ('pressed, but the machine does not see it yet' / 'the machine sees it; press "I did it" to go on') and the wait continues. New portal route /api/dvt/acted -> portalDvtActed, delivered to the runner once (like an answer) and handed to the script by A.ackAct.

Timed holds start from the press. DVT-SAF-008: 'PULL the door firmly and keep pulling, then press I am pulling' and 'HOLD THE MAGNET against the door sensor ... press I am holding it' now begin their ten seconds when the person confirms - until now the window ran whether or not anybody had a hand on the door or a magnet on the sensor, and the recorded lock_engaged / defeat_by_magnet_possible could come from an empty bench.

A step the machine witnesses by itself is shown WITHOUT a button, because a press would add nothing to the measurement: the UV-off timing ('OPEN THE DOOR NOW', timed from the door sensor) and the machine bench's own prompts. Bench prompts (sCureBox-CS :3002, e.g. 'DISCONNECT THE HEATER THERMISTOR NOW') now reach the site as the step instead of being buried in the status line; the bench has no route to take a confirmation yet - noted in DVT/README.md as the one gap left.

The simulated operator in DVT/web/dvt-auto.test.cjs presses too, from inside the machine poll (the scripts' waits run on virtual time, so a real-time timer never got a turn); all 39 guided scripts still play through, DVT-SAF-008 records its 14 values with 14 presses and leaves nothing on.

Tests: the press round trip and the refusal to press a machine-watched step (test_code.cjs), the press reaching the engine through the runner (runner.test.cjs), and the phone QA - the button is 48 px, it sends, it cannot be pressed twice, and a machine-watched step shows no button (test_phone.cjs, 54 checks).

DVT portal: the step the person has to do now is the headline, not a grey line. A guided script can publish an instruction with c.act() (dvt-auto.js) instead of c.say(); the runner sends it to the site as its own field with the seconds left and the stage it belongs to, and the run card shows it big and amber in 'What to do now' - 'OPEN THE DOOR and keep it open · 24 s · step 4 of 6' - and marks it 'DO NOW:' in the run log. Every waiting prompt of DVT-SAF-008 (open / close / pull the door, hold the magnet, hold the door closed, the UV-off 'OPEN THE DOOR NOW') now goes out this way.

Why: on 2026-10-29 DVT-SAF-008 failed with 'the machine did not see the door open'. The runner had asked for the door at 21:00:49, but the instruction reached the portal as an ordinary status line while the big box said 'The test is running by itself - nothing to do. Stay clear of the machine' - so nobody opened the door and the 30 s wait timed out. The door reading itself was correct.

A run that ends (done / failed / cancelled, or stopped from the site) clears its step, so no finished card is left telling someone to open a door. dvt_requests gains an 'act' column (added at the end, existing sheets migrate in place); PORTAL_BUILD 0.9.145 makes open tabs reload.

Pass criteria short-circuit in the JavaScript evaluator too (dvt-criteria.js), matching criteria.py from 0.9.112: one conjunct that is definitely false makes the run FAIL even when a later field was never recorded. The Python/JS parity test caught the mismatch.
The local console (dvt-tool.html) shows the same instructions in 17 px amber, and dvt-catalog.js was rebuilt for catalog 0.58.

Tests: the step's round trip through the portal (test_code.cjs), the runner sending it and clearing it at the end (runner.test.cjs), and the phone QA checking it is the headline, amber, with the countdown and the stage, and never says 'nothing to do' while it waits (test_phone.cjs - 50 checks).

DVT console: alarms are pulled from the machine (SRS-DVT-198). A procedure step that records an alarm (alarm_raised / error_code / alarm_text / time_to_alarm - 20 tests) is now witnessed by the console: while the step is open it reads the machine's active-alarm list from /api/state, keeps the first appearance of every code with the seconds from the step's start, and writes the code, the machine's own text and that time into the run. Next stays locked until an alarm is seen; 'No alarm appeared' records alarm_raised = false (the run commits FAIL, not BLOCKED) and 'No link to the machine' (offered only while it is unreachable, for DVT-SAF-010 / 014) records the step by hand and logs that the console did not witness it. New dvt_tool/alarms.py, card 'Alarms from the machine' in the wizard, every alarm seen is a campaign event.

Why: on 2026-10-29 DVT-SAF-003 ran with a fixed 10 kOhm resistor in place of the chamber NTC. The firmware's frozen-reading rule (Err 9006) never fired - it asks for less than 0.01 C of movement in 90 s at >= 50 % output, while the reading's own quantisation is 0.0043 C and a steady input wanders ~0.02 C over that window (measured on the unit, 154 samples) - so the heater kept driving and the wizard walked on to the next step with nothing recorded. The firmware rule itself is unchanged here, pending a decision on frozen_reading.min_delta_c / min_duty_pct.

DVT catalog 0.58: new step key expect_alert - the error codes the console must see on that step - declared where the firmware or the error registry pins the code (DVT-SAF-002 9010/9001, DVT-SAF-003 9006, DVT-SAF-004 9011-9014/9050, DVT-SAF-006 9034/9003, DVT-SAF-017 9007); validated at load. A code that appears but is not the declared one does not lock the step: what the machine really raised is recorded and flagged red for the verdict page. The other 15 tests with alarm fields are watched generically until their code is confirmed (Open Issues in docs/SRS-DVT-Tool.md).

DVT DUT reader fixed: the firmware's alerts: [9011] + alertDetails shape is now understood (it only spoke the simulator's [{code, message}], so alarm_text was always empty against a real machine), and doorOpen is derived from the firmware's doorClosed - the wizard header said 'door closed' when it simply did not know.

DVT pass criteria short-circuit like Python: one conjunct that is definitely false makes the run FAIL even when a later field was never recorded (a silent machine is a result, not missing data). An undecided criterion is still BLOCKED.

DVT simulator speaks the machine's error codes (registry 90xx / 6016 instead of the retired 1xxx-2xxx numbers) and gains a 'heater sensor replaced by a fixed resistor' fault: the reading sticks where it was fitted, the real chamber keeps climbing and 9006 follows 90 s later, so DVT-SAF-003 can be rehearsed without hardware. Three faults still have no registry code (mains dropout, thermal cutout, LED over-temperature) - listed as Open Issues.

Tests: 12 new cases in DVT/tests/test_dvt_tool.py - both alert shapes, the gate, a wrong code, an alarm already active when the step opened, a silent machine committing FAIL, record-by-hand, the catalog declarations, the frozen-reading alarm end to end on the simulator, and the wizard itself (Next refused on DVT-SAF-003's alarm step until the console sees 9006, then the fields, the run values and the campaign event are filled by the console).

Error editor (tools/error-editor.html): each error's title is editable and has a 'Repair video URL' field (https only; a link to preview it, a Video badge on the card, a 'legacy' tag on the grouped codes no longer raised) - the service team sets one video per code.

Per-component error codes from firmware 1.0.106 (one per thermistor, fan and LED panel: 9010-9014, 9020-9025, 9030-9034, 9040-9045, 9060-9065) added to public/config/errors.json (4.0.0, videoUrl on every error); the cure screen and Settings compare families (src/lib/error-codes.ts) so 9010 and the old 9001 both open the heater fault, every 902x / 903x fan alert pauses the cure, and an LED panel that does not heat raises its own code (9040 / 9041 / 9044 / 9045).

sCure Cloud 'Errors today': the title of each code comes from the registry (cloud/google/ErrorRegistry.gs, generated by build_errors.py from errors.json) and a code with a repair video gets a 'Video' link (new tab). Tests: test_code.cjs (title + video per alert) and test_errors_page.cjs (browser).

QA tool: 'One Error Code Per Component + Repair Video' checks every per-component code (title names its part, family severity, troubleshooting, videoUrl empty or https) and the family rules of the cure screen; SRS §9 lists the new codes.

sCure Cloud DVT run window: once a run is queued it shows What to do now for each stage (wait for the runner / press Start at the CureBox / answer the question / nothing to do while it runs / the result and the next step), the CureBox status from its last sync (online, chamber temperature, door, UV, heating, cooling, sync age) and a timed run log of every status, machine line and question.

tools/error-editor.html showed the critical / warning counts but an empty list (user, 2026-10-21): it was written for codes like 'E-1001' and split each code on '-'; the registry now uses plain numbers (9007), so drawing the first card threw and nothing appeared. Codes are read as text now (E / W shown from the severity), the title comes from 'message' (was 'title'), every shown field is HTML-escaped, and the error's layer is shown with the other locked fields.

Step 4 of the help names both copies: sCureBox-CS/config/errors.json (the machine's alert screen - needs a firmware install) and sCure-A/public/config/errors.json (the web app). Checked in Chrome with both real files: 15 critical + 33 warnings drawn, every field of every error kept on load.

sCure Cloud DVT guide window stays open after Queue: a status bar under the title follows the run live (queued, waiting at the machine, running, done / failed with the verdict), shows the machine's questions with their answer buttons and a Stop the run button; Cancel becomes Close, a click outside no longer closes it once a run is queued, and Run again re-queues after it ends.

sCure Cloud DVT tab: Run on a test now opens a guide window first - purpose, safety plan, equipment, what to prepare, the numbered procedure and the pass criteria - with Cancel / Queue on <CureBox>; nothing is queued until Queue is pressed (Esc or a click outside closes it).

sCure Cloud DVT guide window: a Simulation area - Simulate a passing / failing run plays the procedure steps and checks the pass criteria against made-up readings (a small criteria evaluator: AND/OR/NOT, comparisons, max/min/abs, catalog thresholds), showing each check and the simulated verdict; nothing is sent or recorded.
sCure Cloud sign-in: pressing Enter in the password field signed in but left the page on Sign in (the focused field counted as 'busy', so the page never redrew); it now opens the portal.

A CureBox is one unit (user, 2026-10-12: 'there is only one machine'): the DVT tab of a CureBox shows only its own unit - the one its DVT runner is set to and the ones it has runs of - and no unit row when that is a single unit; the catalog's other UUTs are the campaign plan and appear only under All CureBoxes.

On 2026-10-14 a tab left open from before that change queued DVT-SAF-007 for UUT-02 on CureBox-1 (cancelled). Now the portal refuses a request for a unit other than the one the CureBox's runner reported ('CureBox-1 is unit UUT-01 - reload the page'), the runner refuses one too before any dialog, and the page shows 'This page is out of date - Reload' when the portal was deployed after the tab was opened (PORTAL_BUILD).
Tests: test_code.cjs (other-unit request refused, build reported) and runner.test.cjs (other-unit request refused before the confirmation).

Run DVT tests from sCure Cloud, confirmed at the machine (user, 2026-10-12: 'there is no option to start a test' - 'we confirm the start at the machine'). In the DVT tab of a CureBox every automated test has a Run button and the unit has 'Run all open tests'; the request goes to a queue in Code.gs (dvt_requests) and the DVT runner on that CureBox takes it. Nothing turns on until someone at the machine presses Start on its screen: Decline, no answer in 10 minutes, or Cancel on the site mean the test never starts.

While a test runs the site shows its live line, and a step that needs a person (open the door, pull a sensor, read a meter) is asked in the request's row with Done / Yes / No / Skip or a value box - the answer goes back to the machine. Cancel stops a running test (the engine turns everything off). The panel shows whether the CureBox's runner is online.

DVT/runner/dvt-runner.cjs: the runner. It loads the very dvt-catalog.js / dvt-criteria.js / dvt-auto.js the DVT tool uses (one engine, no second copy of the tests), refuses a machine busy with a process and tests without an automatic script, asks for the confirmation through the firmware (127.0.0.1:3001/api/dvt/remote-confirm), relays prompts and answers, records the verdict with the catalog's criteria and uploads the run and its raw samples under its CureBox. install-runner.sh (on the machine, sudo) installs it as the scure-dvt-runner service; deploy-runner.ps1 packs, copies and installs it from the PC.

Tests: test_code.cjs covers the queue (no duplicates, oldest first, one machine's queue, waiting / prompt / answer handed over once / cancel before and during a run / done with verdict); DVT/runner/runner.test.cjs covers Start, Decline, expiry, cancel before Start and while running, a busy machine, a manual test and the hello + catalog (pytest drives it and checks the confirmation comes before the engine); QA mirror 'DVT From The Site: Nothing Runs Without Start At The Machine'.

sCure Cloud shows each CureBox's NetBird state on its machine card (user, 2026-10-12: 'can the API ping the machine?'). NetBird's API has no ping, but its peer list says whether a peer is connected and when it was last seen; Code.gs reads it read-only (GET /api/peers, cached 30 s) with a NetBird token and maps each CureBox to its peer name (NETBIRD_TOKEN / NETBIRD_PEERS, or the git-ignored secrets file through build_secrets.py). Of several registrations of one machine (a reflash re-enrols it) the connected / newest one counts; the rest are reported as stale.

The pill reads 'NetBird connected' or 'NetBird offline · seen <date>', and its tooltip says what the pair of states means: syncing here but off NetBird = the machine runs, remote access (SSH, screen) is down; off both = no power or no network. First reading: CureBox-1 has been off NetBird since 2026-10-09 20:42 UTC while it keeps syncing, and three stale registrations of it sit in the NetBird dashboard.

The web app needs the external-request permission for this (script.external_request); the owner approved it in the editor before the deploy, so machine sync never stopped (checked live: CureBox-1 online after the deploy).
Tests: test_code.cjs covers the newest-registration choice, the 30 s cache, and a refused token shown as an error; the live QA (28 checks) covers the pill on the real portal.

The portal's DVT tab is laid out like the DVT tool (user, 2026-10-12: 'why is it not broken down this way, why do all the tests show in the tool'): the five counters (runs owed / pass / fail / blocked / open) and the progress bar for the chosen unit, then every phase with its gate and P / F / B / owed counts, and inside it EVERY test the catalog owes on that unit - recorded or not - with its status, safety-critical / auto badges, done / owed runs and the time estimate. A test opens to its owed runs (variant, repetition, verdict, operator, date), a run opens to its values and raw files.

Why the tab had only 13 tests: the portal knew only the runs that were uploaded, not the catalog. The DVT tool now publishes its catalog (kind 'dvt_catalog': phases, gates, and per test its units and the variant|rep runs it owes) on its first sync and on every Sync all; Code.gs keeps it in the dvt_catalog sheet and serves it with the runs. Runs the current catalog no longer owes (an older catalog's repetitions) are listed under 'Other uploaded runs' instead of being counted, so the numbers match the tool.
Each run shows the date it was recorded in the tool, not when it reached the portal (v11 of the web app).

DVT-SAF-014 no longer waits on a heartbeat stop that never happened. Pressing Done after 'stop the heartbeat now' proved nothing: on the unit nobody had stopped anything, the heartbeat file was 0 s old, the watchdog was armed with nothing to cut, and the card waited on as if the watchdog had failed. After Done the runner now checks for ten seconds that the firmware really went silent (the API lives in the firmware process); if it is still answering the run stops with that said plainly and how to freeze the process. The automatic runner no longer refuses to start after a program has ended. /api/state keeps the last program in `recipe` after it finishes, and P.idle treated any state other than 'idle' as a running process - so one aborted SAF-012 attempt ('Aborted by operator') made every script say 'a process is running on the machine - stop it first' with nothing running. Only a program that is still going (running, paused, starting, preflight, waiting) counts now.

DVT-SAF-013 finds the trip when the recording starts with the body already hot. The second run on the unit began at 255 C, climbed 7 C to 262.6, tripped, fell 62 C and climbed again - and the 0.9.35 rule (the peak must stand 20 C above the low before it) rejected that trip as a cooling tail, so the recording never stopped. The trip is now recognised by some climb before it (3 C) and a big drop after it (20 C): a cooling tail at the start has no climb and is still skipped, a hot start is found. When a run starts hot, time_to_trip is measured from the start of the recording, not from ambient - only a run started cold gives the true time.

DVT-SAF-013 stops as soon as it has its three numbers. autoStop waited ten minutes after the trip before looking for the reset - a leftover from the chamber fields the test no longer has - so a run that had already tripped and reset kept recording. It now stops the moment the body climbs 2 C above its low after the trip and holds it for 20 s (the cutout closed), or 20 minutes after the trip if it never does. autoStop also writes the graph marks from the live trace every tick, so the lines follow the current run. Step 4 of the catalog says the same in both languages.

Steps that need the door closed to start (2 and 3) first ask 'close the door to continue to step N'; the others count down 3 s with a ■ to stay put. A step that did not pass stays where it is and the log says which clause failed. Step 1 (the cure with the door open) advances to step 2 the same way. DVT-SAF-013 finishes itself (user: 'I do not want to stop the process - it should do everything and tell me it completed successfully'). DVT_AUTO.autoStop watches the stored samples once a second from the TC-08 card: not before the trip, not in the ten minutes after it, and then the moment the body climbs again (the cutout closed), or twenty minutes after a trip with no reset - the catalog step, applied by the tool. The card stops the recording itself, reads the trace, and DVT_AUTO.completed records the verdict when every criteria field is filled, through the page's own evaluator and thresholds, so the sentence the operator reads - 'the test finished on its own and PASSED - CUT-OFF at 128.3 °C after 4.97 min, closed again at 31.6 °C' - says PASSED or FAILED exactly as the recorded verdict does, never 'successfully' on a failing run.

The cutout's rated trip temperature is the one value the verdict needs that no trace supplies, so the recording refuses to start without it (DVT_AUTO.prepare) instead of finishing thirty minutes later with a field to come back for. The page hooks (0.9.37) are guarded, so a page without these functions still records by hand.

Results folder: a recording could silently stop reaching the folder. Stopping a recording whose trace is not on disk says so out loud (log + dialog: reconnect the folder before closing the page)

DVT-SAF-013 pass criterion, as the user stated it: the heater body may not pass the cutout's rated trip temperature by more than 10 % - `cutout_trip_temp <= rated_trip_temp * 1.1`, in place of the +/-10 C band. Both criteria evaluators already handle multiplication; the console test covers 9.6 % over (pass), 12 % over (fail), an early trip (pass) and a missing rating (blocked).

DVT-SAF-013's first real run on the unit read the wrong turn. The body was still cooling from an earlier attempt when the recording started - 78.9 C falling to 73.2 in the first twenty seconds - and the analyser took that dip for the cut-off: trip 78.91 C, time to trip 0 min, reset 73.23 C, while the graph beside them plainly showed the climb to 260 C and the trip eleven minutes in. The turn detector now takes a `minRise`: the peak has to stand at least that far above the lowest point before it, and a dip that does not is passed over and the search restarts from its bottom. SAF-013 asks for 20 C - a cutout trip is a real climb, never a dip - so the first climb-then-fall is the one returned. The synthetic run in trace-check.cjs now starts the same way the real one did, so this exact mistake fails the suite.
Press 'Read the recording again' on the run already made: the stored trace is re-read with the corrected detector and the three numbers and the marks come out right without repeating the heat-up.

DVT-SAF-013 has one way to run it. The whole-test 'Run the test' card at the top of the run was a second path to the same recording the tc08_record card on step 2 already makes - and it still carried the old nine-step intro, still stopped for prompts about fields the test no longer has, and stopped on the operator when the two paths crossed. The user runs it from step 2 and it works; the top card is gone for this test (37 scripts now). Step 2 is the path: the card switches the heater fan on, refuses a floating probe, records CH1 with the chamber and the machine's own heater command, and on stop reads the three numbers and draws the graph.

The two remaining scripts that read fan tachs read them the way the machine reports them. DVT-THM-005 (tach_rpm) and DVT-SAF-019 (baseline_tach, tach_reading, tach_at_alarm) read fanRpm[FAN_x], which the machine keys by ROLE - on the unit those fields were recorded empty while the fans spun. Both now go through DVT_AUTO.P.rpm (0.9.32): fanRpmEach by fan first, then the group reading where the group is that one fan. P.rpm's role map is corrected on the way - FAN_COOLING is the chamber_intake group, not led_cooling, which is the four LED fans and so never a single fan's exact reading - and the old-host fallback (fanRpm keyed by fan name) is dropped.

The simulated machine in DVT/web/dvt-auto.test.cjs now reports fanRpm by role and fanRpmEach by fan exactly as the unit does, which is why the harness had agreed with the bug until now; a new test asserts both scripts still measure their tachs against that shape and that no script reads fanRpm[<fan>] directly.

The heater fan was reported as 'not turning' on every DVT-SAF-013 start although it ran at 3600 rpm: the recording's prepare step read fan speed as fanRpm[FAN_HEATER], but the machine keys fanRpm by role (led_cooling, chamber_intake, chamber_heating) and puts the per-fan names in fanRpmEach, so the tach came back null and the recording (and the fan row on the TC-08 card) refused. New helper DVT_AUTO.P.rpm(state, fan) reads fanRpmEach first, then the role's reading (exact for FAN_HEATER and FAN_COOLING, the only fans of their groups), then the old host's fan-keyed shape; the SAF-013 prepare uses it. The same wrong read in DVT-THM-005 and DVT-SAF-019, and the script simulator that agreed with it, are the next entry

DVT-SAF-013 on the TC-08 card: with the heater fed from the external supply the machine never reports heating, so the open-thermocouple rule (CH1 far above the cold junction while nothing runs) marked a genuinely hot heater body (182 C) as an open probe, Start stayed disabled, and neither the fan nor the recording ever started. Heater fan for an external heater runs from the moment the TC-08 is seen on the machine, not only once Start is pressed: a fifth readiness row shows it turning on, its rpm, or why it did not start (retried every 10 s, e.g. through the start-up UV self-test); Start needs it green. The fan goes back to the machine when the recording stops

The TC-08 graph is live: the card draws its canvas as soon as the recording starts and adds a point every second (heater body and chamber against minutes), instead of showing only the previous run until the recording was stopped

DVT-SAF-013 trimmed to what its graph gives (user, 2026-09-27). The test used to carry 22 data fields and a nine-step procedure written for a machine that removes its own software limits; the machine cannot do that and the user drives the heater from an external supply instead. The catalog block is rewritten around that in both languages - purpose, safety plan, equipment, preconditions, four procedure steps - and the data fields are now five: rated_trip_temp (the one value typed in, the reference the trip is judged against) and four read out of the TC-08 trace on stop - time_to_trip from where the body started climbing, cutout_trip_temp at the rise-to-fall turn, reset_temp where the body climbed again, and graph_attached. Pass criteria: the trip within 10 C of the rating, a positive time to trip, and the graph. reset_temp is recorded, not judged.

The graph is the fourth deliverable. The TC-08 card draws the recording whenever the run holds one: heater body (CH1) in blue and chamber in orange against minutes, with the heating onset, the cut-off and the reset marked as dashed lines, and the three numbers in the corner. The analyser stores the marks it read (onset, trip, reset, in seconds) with the run, so the graph and the values cannot disagree.

The process figure for SAF-013 (dvt_tool/figures.py, docs/figures/DVT-SAF-013.svg) is redrawn for the four steps: the machine's controller and SSR shown off throughout, the heater fed past them, the cutout the only thing that opens. Everything the analyser still knows how to derive from the trace - chamber overshoot, cooling rate, the machine's own protection - is kept in the stored recording and in the run's JSON, just no longer as catalog fields.

The note written into limits_removed_how follows the operator's language. It was filled in English on a Hebrew page - a value the tool writes into the record on the operator's behalf has to read the way the rest of their screen does, or it looks like somebody else's text pasted into their run.

The page says which version of itself is running, next to the catalog line. The tool is opened straight off disk (file:///.../DVT/web/dvt-tool.html), so a browser that serves a cached dvt-auto.js shows yesterday's behaviour with today's file on disk - and there was no way to tell the two apart. Now there is: if the number shown is not the current one, the browser is serving a cached copy and a hard reload (Ctrl+Shift+R) fixes it.

A recording already in hand can be read again. The analysis used to run only at the moment a recording stopped, so a run measured before an improvement to it kept its empty fields for good. The TC-08 card now offers 'Read the recording again' whenever the run holds samples and has not been recorded yet, which re-runs the current analysis over the stored trace - no need to repeat a two-hour test to benefit from a better reading of it.

DVT-SAF-013 leads with the three numbers the test exists for. The result line now opens with the cut-off temperature, how long the heating took to reach it and the temperature the cutout closed again at, before the detail: 'CUT-OFF at 128.3 C after 4.97 min of heating, closed again at 31.6 C'. Everything else the trace gives is still recorded, but it is no longer what the operator has to read past.

The heater fan is switched on before the recording starts and released when it stops. The heat in this test comes from an external supply the machine knows nothing about, so it never runs the fan on its own - and an element driven with no airflow is a different failure from the one under test. The recording refuses to start if the fan does not turn (page hooks DVT_AUTO.prepare / DVT_AUTO.finish).
CH1 is accepted up to 400 C, following the machine (sCureBox 1.0.46). At 250 the reading stopped where a cutout rated up to 250 C actually trips.

The TC-08 readiness gate rejects an open thermocouple too. 0.9.24 stopped the automatic runner from recording a floating probe, but the card the operator actually uses still showed CH1 green at 249.2 C with the instrument's own terminal block at 24.5 C and said 'everything is connected - you can start'. It now applies the same rule as DVT_AUTO.P.tcCheck: an in-band reading more than 60 C above the cold junction while nothing is heating and no UV is on marks CH1 red, keeps Start disabled, and says the thermocouple is open or badly seated rather than hot - with both numbers shown, so it is obvious why.
The readiness poll now also reads /api/state, since the rule only applies while nothing is running: the same 249 C during a real heat-up is a genuine reading and is left alone.

An open thermocouple is refused instead of being recorded as a temperature. A disconnected or badly seated TC-08 probe does not read null - it floats near the top of the driver's valid band, and the unit sitting at room temperature was seen reading 249.31 C, which is inside -25..250 and would have gone into a run as a real near-cutout body temperature (and, being within 5 C of DVT-SAF-013's 250 C abort ceiling, would have recorded manual_abort_used as true on a test nobody had started).

The cold junction is the reference the check needed: the TC-08's own terminal block sits at ambient, so a probe reading more than 60 C above it while nothing is heating and no UV is on is open, not hot, and the run stops with that said in plain words. The same reading once something IS running is left alone, so a genuine hot body is never refused. DVT-SAF-013 and DVT-GAS-007, the two tests that cannot be measured at all without a trustworthy CH1, now start with this check instead of only testing for a null reading.

DVT-SAF-004 is no longer scripted in dvt-auto.js: it is run by the machine-side DVT bench (catalog tool: bench), which times the heater-body turn on the machine's own clock instead of across the network. One test, one path, no second card - and the 39 scripts become 38.
DVT/tests/test_dvt_web.py: SAF-004 joins OPT-001, OPT-002 and SAF-012 in the set of tests driven by their own cards, so the assertion that every other catalog test has a script keeps its teeth.

DVT-SAF-004 (heater thermistor disconnected) runs by itself from the DVT web page: one Start button hands the whole test to the DVT bench process on the machine (sCureBox 1.0.42, port 3002) - it heats, waits for the heater body to rise, shows DISCONNECT / RECONNECT prompts, takes the instant of the disconnection from the machine's own sensor state, times the heater-body turn, records the alarm and whether its text says to check the cable, sends a heat command that must be refused, and checks heating does not resume by itself. All 10 fields are filled and locked; the 5 Hz trace (heater body, chamber, firmware state) and a graph with the marks go to the results folder. The operator's only actions are pulling and reconnecting the plug
Catalog: SAF-004 step 1 text (EN + HE), tool: bench; the page derives the bench address from the machine address (port 3002) and says so when the machine's software is too old for it
Checked end to end against the bench process in simulation: page -> bench -> prompts -> 10 fields (heater off 0.0 s after the disconnect, alarm 9001 in 0.01 s, heat refused, no resume) -> graph saved

DVT-SAF-013 stops asking the operator for what the recording already shows. Sixteen fields now come out of the trace instead of four. manual_abort_used is read from where the body turned: the test's own safety plan puts the operator's abort at 250 C, so a turn far below it is the cutout doing its job and not somebody stopping the run. heater_power_removed is read from the fall after that turn - a heater body cannot fall while its element is still delivering heat, which is the same evidence this campaign uses for every other shutdown.

The question 'how were the software temperature limits removed?' is gone, and so is 'are the production limits back?'. They were questions about something that never happens: the heater is driven externally, so the machine's limits stand untouched for the whole run, and limits_removed_how, limits_restored and heater_command_percent are all answers to that one fact.

resume_requires_ack is filled only when the answer is unambiguous - the cutout closed again, heat was available, and the machine's drive stayed off, so something held it off. When the drive did come back the tool cannot see whether the operator acknowledged an alarm on the screen first, so that case is left to them rather than recorded as a failure they may not have had.

A run with the heater driven externally now also proves what the machine's own protection did. Each tc08_record row carries the machine's heater command as well (columns t_s, ch1_c, machine_chamber_c, machine_heating, alerts, heater_commanded, heater_pwm_pct), and the analyser reads it: if the machine was commanding heat of its own, the instant its drive goes low while the thermocouple keeps climbing is the protection acting, and the card says so - at what body and chamber temperature it let go, and that the body kept rising afterwards because the remaining heat is external. If it was commanding heat and never let go, that is reported as a finding. If it was not commanding heat at all, the card says plainly that nothing in the run tests its heater cut-off, so nobody reads coverage into a run that has none.
Where the run does show it, heater_off_time, heater_off_delay, heater_off_at_alarm and heater_body_drop_observed are filled from the same trace.
fromTrace no longer throws away the values it had already measured when a later part of the analysis fails: it keeps them, locks them, and reports what went wrong alongside them.

The TC-08 recording fills the run by itself. DVT-SAF-013 is operator-driven - the heater is bridged in hardware because the machine has no no-setpoint heat command - so the TC-08 log is the only record of what happened, and until now it was written to the results folder and nothing read it: steps 4 and 6 to 8 sat there as empty boxes. Stopping the recording now runs DVT_AUTO.fromTrace over the samples and fills what the trace genuinely determines - cutout_trip_temp and chamber_temp_at_trip from the rise-to-fall turn of CH1, time_to_trip measured from where the body actually started climbing (the machine's own heating flag stays false throughout, since the heater is not under its control), chamber_time_to_peak, chamber_overshoot_after_trip and chamber_cooling_rate_after_trip over the five minutes after that peak, self_resetting and reset_temp from the body climbing a second time when the cutout closes, and alarm_raised, error_code and time_to_alarm. Eleven values, all locked against typing, and the card says how many it read.

The alarm is read back out of the trace rather than off the screen: each tc08_record row now carries the machine's alert codes ([t_s, ch1_c, machine_chamber_c, machine_heating, alerts]) and the recording names its own CSV columns, so the header always matches the row.

What the trace cannot tell apart is still the operator's: a body trace looks identical whether the cutout opened or somebody pulled the power, so manual_abort_used and heater_power_removed (which needs the DMM at the SSR output) stay manual, as do limits_restored and post_test_functional_pass.

DVT-SAF-013 says what the machine can and cannot do. Step 3 of the catalog asks for the heater ON at 100 % with no setpoint, and there is no such command anywhere: every heat command the machine accepts takes a setpoint and is clamped to 80 C (RecipeValidator HeatTargetMin 30 / TempMax 80) and nothing reaches the heater SSR past that. The old prompt read as though the tool or the page would send it, so the SSR was never commanded and the operator was left waiting. The card now states plainly that the machine cannot do this and that the heater has to be driven in hardware, at the SSR or the heater supply, before Done is pressed. Decision of the user (2026-09-27): the runner does NOT gain a way to drive the heater past its limits - this test stays operator-driven and the runner only measures.

The StarBright is never read in parallel with anything else: the SAF-017 interlock timing used to fetch /api/dvt/meter and /api/state together, and concurrent callers interleave control transfers on the meter's USB handle (seen wedging it with LIBUSB_ERROR_IO on the unit). The two reads are now sequential.

The automatic runner takes ambient from the instrument too: every script that records ambient_temp (THM-001, THM-002, THM-003, THM-005, SAF-013, GAS-007) now reads the TC-08's own cold junction through /api/dev/picolog/status `ambient` (sCureBox 1.0.39+) rather than the chamber sensor, which was never the room temperature. With no TC-08 on the machine it falls back to the chamber sensor at rest and writes which of the two it used into the run's timeline, so a fallback is never mistaken for a measurement.
DVT/tests/test_dvt_web.py: a test that no script asks the operator for ambient_temp while a probe is on the machine (17 tests, all passing).

DVT-SAF-012 step 2: the operator opens the door with the UV on - the page no longer has the machine release the door (that switched the UV off first). Prompt 'THE UV IS ON - OPEN THE DOOR NOW'; needs sCureBox 1.0.38. The decay graph starts 2 s before the door opens so the lit level shows
The page says 'the machine software does not have <endpoint> - install a newer sCureBox' instead of a bare 'Not found' when the machine is older than the page
Catalog: SAF-012 step 2 text (EN + HE) follows

SAF-013 TC-08 card: ambient_temp is filled and locked from the TC-08's own cold junction (/api/dev/picolog/status ambient, sCureBox 1.0.39+) instead of being typed - a fourth readiness row shows it; on older machine software the field stays for the operator (it had been showing the chamber temperature)

DVT automatic runner (DVT/web/dvt-auto.js): one "Run the test" button per DVT test, at the top of the run. It drives the machine over its own API, logs /api/state at 1-5 Hz (plus the TC-08 on /api/dev/picolog/status and the StarBright on /api/dvt/meter), reads the moments that matter out of the trace - the heater-body rise-to-fall turn, the first new alert code, the settling of a panel - and writes every value it can measure straight into the run. Measured fields are locked against typing, every trace is kept as its own rec.autos entry with its own CSV in the results folder, and a run whose criteria are all measured records its verdict by itself.

39 of the 42 catalog tests have a script (the two UV linearity rows and SAF-012 keep their own cards). A script stops for the operator only where the catalog needs a physical act with no API (pull a connector, apply a magnet, seat a build head), an instrument that is not on the network (clamp meter, O2 analyser, hipot set) or a human judgement (visible damage) - one prompt at a time, inside the card, at the moment it is needed rather than as a form afterwards.

DVT-SAF-013 is deliberately not automated end to end: the runner never removes the software temperature limits, it asks the operator to do that and to command the heater, and measures the cutout from there. Every script turns the machine off when it ends, including on an error or a stop.
